title: Sriracha Chicken Tacos
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.notes: Settled line; 680.4 g source basis carried through.

1 tbsp sriracha = 15 g (Huy Fong label basis 1 tsp = 5 g); 4 tbsp = 60 g source. Not a form flip: sriracha IS a sauce, so 'Sriracha sauce' is a rename onto the existing vocabulary row Sriracha [sriracha], with no change of product, price class or gram weight. Declined the board's generic hot-sauce match, which prices Louisiana-style bottles rather than this chili-garlic paste.
Buy string follows the pre-resolved 21 g source basis (the qty engine weighed the 1 tbsp only, not the extra 2 tsp); flagged in detail.

Whole limes purchased and squeezed, 67 g each, matching the Lime Wedges precedent of weighing whole fruit. Reuse of the live limes id (5 of 7, cheapest 0.25 at Walmart), following the 2026-08-27 'fresh lime juice' and 'Lime Wedges' rulings that price whole limes squeezed. Named 'limes' to match the food-DB row this batch already carries.
Settled line; 1.5 g source basis (about 1 g per tbsp chopped).

ingredients.notes: 1 cup shredded romaine = 47 g (USDA measure); 2 cups = 94 g source. New id proposed to the registrar; 'shredded' is a cut, not a form flip.

ingredients.notes: Corn chosen over flour (listed first, and the vocabulary row is Corn Tortillas); 23.5 g each off the Mission label serving of 2 tortillas = 47 g. The source offers a choice and corn is listed first, so the line resolves to the same-form vocabulary row Corn Tortillas [corn-tortillas]; the board carries tortillas at 7 of 7. Corn and flour are different foods at different gram weights, so only one may be priced and weighed.

db_row_findings: sriracha-chicken-tacos: the food DB already carries 'Corn Tortillas' and the mapper's row DIFFERS on serving_grams, carbs_g. Nothing was written and the existing row stands. On one basis, per 100 g: DB 200.0 cal / 4.0 P / 42.0 C / 2.0 F  vs  mapper 212.8 / 4.3 / 42.6 / 2.1. On one basis (the mapper's row scaled onto the DB's 2 tortillas = 50 g) they still disagree: calories 106.4 vs 100. existing={"serving_grams": 50, "carbs_g": 21} new={"serving_grams": 47, "carbs_g": 20}

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Romaine is not already priced under another spelling: the pre-resolve board matcher returned only the generic `lettuce` id for this term and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it, and no romaine, cos or 'romaine hearts' spelling surfaced in any near-row list for this batch. It is a genuinely different commodity from `lettuce` (iceberg/head basis) on both price and pack - romaine sells as 3-count hearts or a whole head at a clearly higher shelf price - which is the same variety-pricing distinction the estate already enforces for red onion vs onions and cherry tomatoes vs tomatoes. If a romaine id already exists under another name this is a reuse, not a new mint, and the line should take that id.

registrar_rulings.reason: The mapper's central claim - that no romaine spelling exists anywhere in the estate - is false: I read grocery\commodities.json at the `lettuce` id (line 7557) and its include list is ['\blettuce\b', '\biceberg\b', '\bromaine\b'], so romaine heads and hearts are EXPLICITLY claimed by the existing `lettuce` commodity today; the dossier's own near-row list showed this include truncated at '\bromai...'. `lettuce` is live-priced at $0.9975/each across 7 stores (crown: Tanimura & Antle 4-ct at Family Fare), and its excludes ('shredded', 'chopped', 'salad mix', 'kit', 'blend') confirm the intended purchase for a 'shredded romaine lettuce' recipe line is a whole head/hearts you shred yourself - the same purchase `lettuce` prices. Minting `romaine-lettuce` while `lettuce`'s include claims \bromaine\b would put the SAME romaine SKU under two ids with two prices, the exact bread-crumbs/breadcrumbs defect this gate exists to prevent. Follow-up: add `romaine-lettuce -> lettuce` to recipe-floor-id-map.json (units match: each). If Brad later wants the red-onion-style variety split the mapper argues for, that is an estate edit - narrow `lettuce`'s include to drop \bromaine\b, then mint - not something this gate can approve while the overlap stands. Separately, on the vocabulary side: the ingredient NAME 'shredded romaine lettuce' has no vocabulary row per the pre-resolve; if a row is minted, FDC 746769 (Lettuce, cos or romaine, raw, Foundation) is the correct macro source - that is a name-namespace action and does not mint an id.

join_fallbacks: '1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts ()': the qty engine could not ground this weight (count/each guess of 680 g against a line stating 227 g - the engine did not read the stated weight), so its number is a fallback and the cross-check is skipped; recorded to the density gaps list
macro_cross_check: Source page publishes 573 cal / 48 g protein / 33 g carbs per serving at 4 servings. Recomputed at source scale from the food DB plus my three new rows: chicken 680.4 g = 790 cal / 151.9 P; cheddar 113 g = 444 cal / 24.2 P; avocado 150 g = 240 cal; oil 21 g = 180 cal; tortillas 188 g (8) = 400 cal / 8 P / 80 C; sour cream 115 g = 161 cal; sriracha 60 g = 56 cal; limes 134 g = 40 cal; honey 21 g = 60 cal; romaine 94 g = 16 cal; cilantro and salt negligible. Totals 2387 cal / 193.8 g protein / 150 g carbs, i.e. 597 cal, 48.5 g protein, 37.6 g carbs per serving. Protein is within 1% of the source's 48 g, so no portion is misweighed - in particular the 1 1/2 lb chicken line needs no each-weight correction. Calories run 4% high and carbs 14% high, both explained by counting whole limes rather than juice only and by the tortilla label being a touch heavier than the source's assumption. Run band (450-800 cal, protein >= 40) PASSES at 597 / 48.5, and per-serving figures are unchanged by the 3.5x scale to 14 servings.
